package_info.why_malicious: The package is a trojanized clone of a legitimate library, containing hidden code that extracts and executes a command-and-control (C2) backdoor payload from an embedded image file during installation. This enables remote code execution and data exfiltration on victim systems.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code spawns a detached Node.js process to execute the malicious loadformat.js script, enabling further payload execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Spawning a detached process to run an additional script during installation is a common technique for hiding malicious activity and persisting execution outside the main process.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not execute hidden scripts or spawn detached processes during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may run postinstall scripts for setup, but not to execute hidden or obfuscated payloads.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the code reads embedded image files, extracts ASCII payloads hidden in the image bytes, and dynamically executes the extracted code as JavaScript, enabling arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Extracting and executing code from image files is a classic steganography-based evasion technique, highly unusual and dangerous in package installation scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not extract and execute code from image files during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case for executing code extracted from images in a package install context.
key_indicators: Reads and parses image files for ASCII payloads
Conditional logic to trigger payload only if hidden code is present

execution_context.file_location: payload extracted from logo2.jpg via loadformat.js

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the code registers the victim with a remote C2 server, periodically fetches and executes attacker-supplied commands, and exfiltrates command output to the C2 server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Implements a full-featured C2 backdoor, enabling remote code execution and data exfiltration. The use of a hardcoded IP and dynamic command execution is highly indicative of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not establish persistent C2 channels or execute arbitrary remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case for this behavior in a package install context.

attack_chain.action: During installation, index.js spawns a detached process to execute loadformat.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of loadformat.js and image payload extraction

attack_chain.action: loadformat.js reads embedded image files, extracts ASCII payloads, and dynamically executes the extracted code if present.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of C2 backdoor code if payload is found in image

attack_chain.action: Extracted payload (from logo2.jpg) registers the victim with a remote C2, fetches and executes commands, and exfiltrates results.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote control of victim system and data exfiltration

behavioral_signatures: Postinstall script spawns detached child process
Reads and parses image files for ASCII payloads
Dynamically executes code extracted from non-code files
Establishes persistent outbound connections to hardcoded IPs
Executes arbitrary shell commands based on remote input
file_indicators: logo1.jpg, logo2.jpg, logo3.jpg in package root
Obfuscated or unusually large ASCII strings in image files
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that execute postinstall scripts spawning detached processes, especially those that read and parse image files for ASCII payloads and dynamically execute the result. Flag any package that establishes outbound connections to hardcoded IPs (e.g., 85.208.108.29) or that contains non-standard files (e.g., images) in the root directory that are accessed by install scripts. Use static and dynamic analysis to detect code that uses new Function or eval on data extracted from non-code files.
